```{r setup, include=FALSE}
render_started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
library(bdynets)
source("prepare.R", local = TRUE)

plain_output <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  plain_output(gsub("[ \t]+\n", "\n", x, perl = TRUE), options)
})

figure_dir <- tempfile("beijing-tutorial-figures-")
dir.create(figure_dir)
mapping_directory <- tempfile("beijing-field-mapping-")
dir.create(mapping_directory)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.path = file.path(figure_dir, "figure-"),
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 7.5,
  dpi = 150,
  out.width = "100%"
)

case <- list(
  raw_file = "data/raw/output_LinkTDMOE.csv",
  geometry_file = "data/raw/network.html",
  prepared_file = "data/input.rds",
  day = 10L,
  expected_minutes = 0:9,
  interval_minutes = 5L,
  fields = c(
    pair = "link_id_from_to",
    day = "day_no",
    minute = "timestamp_in_min",
    rate = "link_volume_in_veh_per_hour_for_all_lanes"
  ),
  incoming_fields = c(
    pair = "directed_pair",
    day = "simulation_day",
    minute = "source_minute",
    rate = "entry_rate"
  )
)

source_files <- list.files("data", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
source_files <- source_files[!grepl("/basemap-cache/", source_files)]
source_before <- tools::md5sum(source_files)
full_standard <- readRDS(case$prepared_file)
```

This tutorial shows the complete workflow expected of a new `bdynets` user:

**understand the source → inspect and validate raw records → construct `standard` with `traffic_input()` → visualize `standard` with `traffic_map()` → validate → export and read back.**

The Beijing-specific code is limited to reading the source fields, matching directed road IDs, and aggregating minute-sampled rates. The public constructor and plotting functions are general `bdynets` interfaces.

## Data, source, and preparation goal

This case uses road performance output from a project traffic simulator, stored in `output_LinkTDMOE.csv`. A matching project network file supplies directed road attributes and longitude–latitude geometry. The records describe **simulation day 10**; they are simulated values rather than measurements from roadside sensors.

Each raw value is an **all-lane hourly entry rate sampled once per minute**. Its unit is `vehicles/hour`. It is not speed, occupancy, vehicle count within one minute, relative load, or congestion by itself.

The preparation goal is to:

1. validate one observation for every directed road–minute key;
2. match source road pairs to directed network geometry;
3. average five consecutive minute-sampled hourly rates;
4. retain the result in `vehicles/hour`;
5. construct the standard `bdynets-traffic-input-v1` object; and
6. map one five-minute frame and summarize change across the day.

```{r source-summary, echo=FALSE}
original_sources <- read.csv("data/original-sources.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  original_sources[c("file", "provider", "role")],
  caption = "Original data sources",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)

source_scope <- data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Directed pairs with minute records",
    "Roads matched to supplied geometry",
    "Directed pairs excluded from drawing",
    "Five-minute frames in one day",
    "Prepared flow unit"
  ),
  Value = c(
    full_standard$provenance$source_pairs,
    nrow(full_standard$roads),
    full_standard$provenance$excluded_pairs,
    length(full_standard$times),
    full_standard$unit
  )
)
knitr::kable(source_scope, caption = "Scope of the complete prepared day", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

All 12,287 source pairs retain native minute records. Of these, 11,742 have matching supplied geometry and can be drawn; 545 are excluded from the geographic display. Exclusion from drawing does not mean that their native observations were zero or missing.

Raw time is the number of minutes since simulation midnight. No calendar date or timezone is supplied. A complete day contains 1,440 source minutes and 288 five-minute frames.

## Raw input, field meanings, and editable configuration

### Configuration to edit for another file

The following block contains the values a user normally changes first: file paths, source day, minute domain, aggregation interval, and column mapping.

```{r configuration}
case <- list(
  raw_file = "data/raw/output_LinkTDMOE.csv",
  geometry_file = "data/raw/network.html",
  prepared_file = "data/input.rds",
  day = 10L,
  expected_minutes = 0:9,
  interval_minutes = 5L,
  fields = c(
    pair = "link_id_from_to",
    day = "day_no",
    minute = "timestamp_in_min",
    rate = "link_volume_in_veh_per_hour_for_all_lanes"
  ),
  incoming_fields = c(
    pair = "directed_pair",
    day = "simulation_day",
    minute = "source_minute",
    rate = "entry_rate"
  )
)
```

`fields` maps source headers to four required roles. Changing a header does not change its measurement meaning; the mapped `rate` field must still contain a nonnegative hourly entry rate.

### Inspect the original-format teaching excerpt

The bundled excerpt contains ten rows for directed pair `27->6632`, simulation day 10, and minutes 0–9. It is deliberately small enough to check by hand.

```{r read-raw}
raw <- read.csv(case$raw_file, check.names = FALSE)
raw
```

```{r raw-field-description, echo=FALSE}
raw_dictionary <- data.frame(
  `Source field` = c(
    "link_id_from_to",
    "day_no",
    "timestamp_in_min",
    "link_volume_in_veh_per_hour_for_all_lanes"
  ),
  Meaning = c(
    "Directed endpoint pair, for example 27->6632",
    "Simulation day number; day 10 in this example",
    "Whole minute counted from simulation midnight",
    "All-lane hourly entry rate, in vehicles/hour"
  ),
  `Standard destination` = c(
    "Matched to edge_id; network edge_index becomes road_id",
    "Retained in provenance metadata",
    "Converted from minutes to frame starts in seconds",
    "Averaged within complete five-minute intervals"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(raw_dictionary, caption = "Raw flow field definitions", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

The CSV has identifiers, times, and values, but no drawing geometry. The network source supplies the road attributes and travel-ordered coordinates.

```{r read-network-and-native}
native <- read_beijing_raw(
  moe_file = case$raw_file,
  geometry_file = case$geometry_file,
  fields = case$fields,
  day = case$day,
  expected_minutes = case$expected_minutes
)
```

```{r show-road, echo=FALSE}
road_columns <- c("edge_index", "edge_id", "from_node_id", "to_node_id", "length_km", "lanes", "speed_limit")
knitr::kable(
  native$roads[road_columns],
  caption = "Road attributes read from the source network",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

`edge_id` is a directed endpoint pair. The `geometry` list-column stores longitude–latitude vertices in travel order. Direction matters: `27->6632` is not interchangeable with `6632->27`.

#### Native source object and readback {.unnumbered}

The intermediate `source.rds` retains native IDs, clocks and observations. This sample snapshot is saved and read back in a temporary directory; the supplied day-level snapshot stays unchanged.

```{r native-source, echo=FALSE}
native_directory <- tempfile("native-source-")
dir.create(native_directory)
native_file <- file.path(native_directory, "source.rds")
stopifnot(!file.exists(native_file))
```

```{r native-source-2, echo=TRUE}
saveRDS(native, native_file, compress = "xz", version = 3)
restored_native <- readRDS(native_file)
```

```{r native-source-3, echo=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(restored_native, native))
native <- restored_native
invisible(capture.output(str(native, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = basename(native_file), schema = native$schema, exact_readback = TRUE),
    caption = "Native source snapshot before standard-input construction", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

The intermediate object retains source detail; the next step constructs the common road, value and time tables.

### Deliberately invalid input and correction

A directed pair and minute must identify exactly one rate. Here the first row is duplicated in memory; the original CSV is not changed.

```{r invalid-input}
bad_raw <- rbind(raw, raw[1, ])
cat(tryCatch(
  {
    beijing_records(
      bad_raw,
      native$roads,
      case$expected_minutes,
      case$fields,
      case$day
    )
    "No error was raised."
  },
  error = conditionMessage
))
```

The readable error identifies the duplicated directed-pair–minute key. Removing the duplicate restores the declared minute domain; `native`, created above from the unchanged source, is the corrected input.

```{r corrected-input-check}
corrected <- beijing_records(
  raw,
  native$roads,
  case$expected_minutes,
  case$fields,
  case$day
)
stopifnot(identical(corrected$minute_rates, native$minute_rates))
data.frame(
  directed_pairs = length(corrected$road_pairs),
  source_minutes = length(corrected$minute),
  duplicate_keys = anyDuplicated(raw[c(case$fields["pair"], case$fields["minute"])]),
  missing_pair_minutes = sum(is.na(corrected$minute_rates))
)
```

An observed value of zero is valid data and remains in the calculation. A missing pair–minute record prevents a complete five-minute mean and is rejected rather than silently treated as zero.

## Convert with the general `bdynets` interface

### Prepare canonical road, flow, and time inputs

Raw formats differ across data owners. Beijing-specific preprocessing therefore stops after it has produced the canonical inputs expected by the package: a `roads` table, a long `flow` table, and frame times.

```{r prepare-canonical-tables}
interval_minutes <- case$interval_minutes
roads <- native$roads

# Match each drawable directed road to the corresponding source pair.
road_rows <- match(roads$edge_id, native$road_pairs)
minute_rates <- native$minute_rates[road_rows, , drop = FALSE]

# Average each complete, aligned group of five minute-sampled rates.
first <- seq.int(1L, length(native$minute), by = interval_minutes)
values <- do.call(cbind, lapply(first, function(i) {
  columns <- i + seq_len(interval_minutes) - 1L
  rowMeans(minute_rates[, columns, drop = FALSE])
}))

# Convert source minutes to standard frame starts in seconds.
starts <- native$minute[first] * 60
roads$road_id <- as.character(roads$edge_index)
flow <- data.frame(
  road_id = rep(roads$road_id, length(starts)),
  time = rep(starts, each = nrow(roads)),
  flow = as.vector(values)
)
```

### Construct `standard` with `traffic_input()`

Once the canonical inputs exist, Beijing and other road-flow datasets use the same public constructor.

```{r construct-standard-input}
standard <- bdynets::traffic_input(
  roads = roads,
  flow = flow,
  times = starts,
  time_labels = sprintf(
    "%02d:%02d",
    starts %/% 3600,
    (starts %/% 60) %% 60
  ),
  interval_seconds = rep(interval_minutes * 60, length(starts)),
  unit = "vehicles/hour",
  title = "Beijing simulated entry flow",
  description = "Five-minute mean of minute-sampled all-lane hourly entry rates.",
  preparation = c(
    "Validate one nonnegative rate per directed pair and source minute.",
    "Join directed endpoint pairs to supplied road geometry.",
    "Average complete aligned groups of five source minutes."
  ),
  provenance = list(
    source_files = native$source,
    source_fields = case$fields,
    day_no = native$day_no,
    operation = "Arithmetic mean of five minute-sampled hourly entry rates."
  )
)
```

<div class="note"><code>bdynets::traffic_input()</code> is the general package constructor. <code>read_beijing_raw()</code> and <code>beijing_records()</code> are Beijing source adapters; they are not required names or interfaces for other datasets.</div>

### What does `standard` contain?

The result is a named list with schema `bdynets-traffic-input-v1`. The complete top-level structure is shown first, followed by the two main tables.

```{r standard-structure}
str(standard, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
```

```{r show-standard, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  standard$roads[c("road_id", "edge_id", "from_node_id", "to_node_id", "length_km", "lanes")],
  caption = "Standard roads table; coordinates remain in the geometry list-column",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  standard$flow,
  caption = "Standard flow table",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Field = c("schema", "crs", "timezone", "interval_seconds", "unit"),
    Value = c(
      standard$schema,
      standard$crs,
      "NULL",
      paste(unique(standard$interval_seconds), collapse = ", "),
      standard$unit
    )
  ),
  caption = "Key metadata retained in standard",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

Four concrete changes occur during conversion:

- **Identifier:** source pair `27->6632` matches the directed network, and network `edge_index=102` becomes standard `road_id="102"`.
- **Time:** source minutes 0 and 5 become standard frame starts 0 and 300 seconds.
- **Value:** each complete group of five hourly rates is averaged.
- **Metadata:** interval width, unit, coordinate reference system, preparation steps, and provenance remain attached to the standard object.

The first interval is:

```text
(60 + 60 + 0 + 0 + 0) / 5 = 24 vehicles/hour
```

The second interval contains five observed zeros, so its result is zero rather than missing. The rates are averaged; they are not summed into a five-minute vehicle count.

#### The shared network and panel interfaces {.unnumbered}

The source road has explicit upstream and downstream node IDs. These support the existing `network_data()` and `network_panel()` interfaces as well as the geographic traffic input. The road ID becomes the panel's edge-unit ID, and the rate values and source-minute clock stay unchanged.

```{r shared-panel, echo=FALSE}
edges <- data.frame(edge_id = standard$roads$road_id, from = as.character(standard$roads$from_node_id),
    to = as.character(standard$roads$to_node_id))
nodes <- data.frame(node_id = unique(c(edges$from, edges$to)))
```

```{r shared-panel-2, echo=TRUE}
network <- network_data(nodes, edges, directed = TRUE, provenance = standard$provenance)
```

```{r shared-panel-3, echo=FALSE}
values <- matrix(NA_real_, length(standard$times), nrow(edges), dimnames = list(NULL, edges$edge_id))
values[cbind(match(standard$flow$time, standard$times), match(standard$flow$road_id, edges$edge_id))] <- standard$flow$flow
```

```{r shared-panel-4, echo=TRUE}
panel <- network_panel(values, standard$times, edges$edge_id, network, unit_type = "edge", measure = "entry rate",
    unit = standard$unit, aggregation = "Mean of five minute-sampled hourly rates", provenance = standard$provenance)
long <- panel_long(panel)
```

```{r shared-panel-5, echo=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(long$unit_id, standard$flow$road_id), identical(long$time, standard$flow$time),
    identical(long$value, standard$flow$flow))
knitr::kable(long[c("unit_id", "time", "value", "observed")], caption = "The same source observations in the existing edge-panel interface", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

The panel uses the constructor's unit-exposure storage default; no lane exposure is inferred and no rate is converted into a count. Geographic drawing retains the source geometry in `traffic_input()`. Data with only a segment ID and coordinates need an explicit source endpoint table before an edge network can be constructed. The interfaces do not infer sensor adjacency or travelled routes.

### Adapt a CSV whose columns have different names

Another data owner may use different headers. The user changes only the source-role mapping; the meaning and the general `traffic_input()` interface remain the same.

```{r renamed-csv}
incoming <- raw
names(incoming)[match(unname(case$fields), names(incoming))] <-
  unname(case$incoming_fields)
incoming_file <- file.path(mapping_directory, "minute-rates.csv")
write.csv(incoming, incoming_file, row.names = FALSE, na = "")

incoming <- as.data.frame(data.table::fread(incoming_file, showProgress = FALSE))
mapped_native <- beijing_records(
  incoming,
  native$roads,
  case$expected_minutes,
  case$incoming_fields,
  case$day
)
stopifnot(identical(mapped_native$minute_rates, native$minute_rates))
```

```{r renamed-csv-display, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(head(incoming), caption = "Equivalent CSV with renamed columns", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Required_role = names(case$incoming_fields),
    Incoming_header = unname(case$incoming_fields)
  ),
  caption = "Explicit mapping for the renamed CSV",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

After the mapping check, the canonical-table code in Section 3.1 and the same `bdynets::traffic_input()` call in Section 3.2 apply without changing the package interface.

## Pass the standard object to `traffic_map()`

The teaching excerpt contains only one road and two frames. For a useful map, the report reads the supplied full-day standard object. This object has the same schema as `standard`; it simply contains all drawable roads and all 288 frames.

```{r full-standard-input}
day_standard <- readRDS(case$prepared_file)
str(day_standard, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)

day_view <- read_traffic(case$prepared_file)
clock_labels <- sub("^.* ", "", day_view$time_labels)
index <- match(params$time_label, clock_labels)
if (is.na(index)) stop("The selected frame is not present in the prepared day.")

if (params$basemap) {
  day_view$basemap <- traffic_basemap(day_view, road_classes = character())
}
options(bdynets.basemap.auto = FALSE)
```

```{r full-standard-preview, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  head(day_standard$flow),
  caption = "First rows of the full-day standard flow table",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

### Road flow map

The first argument to `traffic_map()` is the standard object.

```{r road-map, fig.alt="Beijing simulated road entry rates in the selected five-minute frame; green is lower and red is higher."}
map_result <- traffic_map(
  day_standard,
  index = index,
  basemap = day_view$basemap,
  title = "Beijing simulated entry flow",
  caption = paste0(
    "Frame ", params$time_label,
    "; five-minute mean entry rate in vehicles/hour; missing values are grey."
  )
)
```

The map uses common logarithmic classes across the prepared input. Green denotes lower entry rates; yellow, orange, and red denote progressively higher entry rates. Red indicates a high entry rate, not necessarily congestion. Grey indicates missing data and must not be interpreted as zero.

### Daily mean road flow

```{r road-trend, fig.height=4.4}
trend <- traffic_trend(day_view)
plot(trend, metric = "mean", index = index)
```

The curve is the arithmetic mean of available road values in each frame. Observed zeros contribute to the mean; missing values are excluded. It is not a regional total and should not be read as the number of vehicles entering all roads.

## Validate the conversion and prepared day

The checks below connect the hand calculation, teaching excerpt, complete prepared day, stable identifiers, missingness, and source-file protection.

```{r validation, echo=FALSE}
sample_at <- match(
  paste(standard$flow$road_id, standard$flow$time),
  paste(full_standard$flow$road_id, full_standard$flow$time)
)

validation <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Five-minute values equal the hand calculation",
    "Teaching excerpt agrees with the full prepared day",
    "Full row count equals roads multiplied by frames",
    "Full road_id-time keys are unique",
    "Road IDs are nonmissing, character, and unique",
    "Observed values are finite and nonnegative",
    "Excluded-pair count is source pairs minus drawable roads",
    "Source files remain unchanged during report generation"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    identical(standard$flow$flow, c(24, 0)),
    !anyNA(sample_at) && identical(standard$flow$flow, full_standard$flow$flow[sample_at]),
    nrow(full_standard$flow) == nrow(full_standard$roads) * length(full_standard$times),
    !anyDuplicated(full_standard$flow[c("road_id", "time")]),
    is.character(full_standard$roads$road_id) &&
      !anyNA(full_standard$roads$road_id) &&
      !anyDuplicated(full_standard$roads$road_id),
    all(is.finite(full_standard$flow$flow) & full_standard$flow$flow >= 0),
    full_standard$provenance$excluded_pairs ==
      full_standard$provenance$source_pairs - nrow(full_standard$roads),
    identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files))
  )
)
knitr::kable(validation, caption = "Core validation results", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)

coverage <- data.frame(
  Roads = nrow(full_standard$roads),
  Frames = length(full_standard$times),
  `Interval (minutes)` = unique(full_standard$interval_seconds) / 60,
  `Total records` = nrow(full_standard$flow),
  `Missing records` = sum(is.na(full_standard$flow$flow)),
  `Observed zeros` = sum(full_standard$flow$flow == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  Unit = full_standard$unit,
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(coverage, caption = "Complete-day coverage", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

<div class="result">The workflow is valid only when every row in the validation table is <code>TRUE</code>. The coverage table reports missing values and observed zeros separately.</div>

## Export, read back, and reuse

`write_traffic_input()` publishes a standard object to a **new** directory. It writes the complete R object, readable CSV tables, ordered road vertices, a data dictionary, validation records, source identities, metadata, and checksums. Existing destinations and protected source locations are rejected.

The report performs a small export with the teaching `standard` object so that readback remains fast and directly inspectable.

```{r prepared-export}
prepared_export_dir <- tempfile("beijing-prepared-export-")
dictionary <- read.csv("data/data-dictionary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dictionary_key <- paste(dictionary$table, dictionary$field, sep = "/")
standard_key <- c(
  paste("roads", names(standard$roads), sep = "/"),
  paste("flow", names(standard$flow), sep = "/")
)
dictionary <- dictionary[dictionary_key %in% standard_key, ]

prepared_path <- write_traffic_input(
  standard,
  prepared_export_dir,
  source_files = c(case$raw_file, case$geometry_file),
  native = native,
  dictionary = dictionary
)
restored <- readRDS(prepared_path)
```

```{r prepared-export-checks, echo=FALSE}
metadata <- jsonlite::read_json(
  file.path(prepared_export_dir, "metadata.json"),
  simplifyVector = TRUE
)
exported_flow <- read.csv(
  file.path(prepared_export_dir, "flow.csv"),
  na.strings = metadata$csv$missing,
  colClasses = c(road_id = "character")
)
prepared_manifest <- read.csv(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "checksums.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
core_fields <- setdiff(names(standard), "provenance")

export_checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "RDS core fields read back unchanged",
    "CSV identifiers, times, and values read back correctly",
    "Data dictionary and validation record are present",
    "Prepared-export checksums agree",
    "Source files remain unchanged"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    all(vapply(core_fields, function(key) identical(restored[[key]], standard[[key]]), logical(1))),
    identical(exported_flow$road_id, standard$flow$road_id) &&
      identical(as.numeric(exported_flow$time), as.numeric(standard$flow$time)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(exported_flow$flow, standard$flow$flow, check.attributes = FALSE)),
    file.exists(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "data-dictionary.csv")) &&
      file.exists(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "validation.csv")),
    identical(
      unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(prepared_export_dir, prepared_manifest$file))),
      prepared_manifest$md5
    ),
    identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files))
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(file = sort(list.files(prepared_export_dir))),
  caption = "Files in the prepared-data export",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(export_checks, caption = "Prepared-data readback checks", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  read.csv(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "validation.csv")),
  caption = "Validation and coverage record stored with the export",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

### Export figures and the selected frame

`traffic_export()` uses the same prepared day and selected frame as the on-screen map. It writes PNG and PDF figures, the selected records, summary and trend tables, provenance, session information, input identities, and checksums.

```{r figure-export}
figure_export_dir <- tempfile("beijing-figure-export-")
traffic_export(
  day_view,
  figure_export_dir,
  index = index,
  input_files = c(prepared = case$prepared_file)
)
```

```{r figure-export-checks, echo=FALSE}
figure_manifest <- read.csv(file.path(figure_export_dir, "checksums.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
figure_checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "PNG and PDF map files are present",
    "Selected-frame data and provenance are present",
    "Figure-export checksums agree"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    all(c("map.png", "map.pdf") %in% list.files(figure_export_dir)),
    all(c("selected-frame.rds", "provenance.json") %in% list.files(figure_export_dir)),
    identical(
      unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(figure_export_dir, figure_manifest$file))),
      figure_manifest$md5
    )
  )
)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(file = sort(list.files(figure_export_dir))),
  caption = "Files in the figure export",
  format = "html",
  row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(figure_checks, caption = "Figure-export checks", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

When `params$export` is `TRUE`, the following block also creates persistent copies under `params$export_dir`. The destination must not already exist.

```{r optional-persistent-export}
if (params$export) {
  if (file.exists(params$export_dir)) {
    stop("The requested export directory already exists; choose a new directory.")
  }
  dir.create(params$export_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  write_traffic_input(
    standard,
    file.path(params$export_dir, "prepared-data"),
    source_files = c(case$raw_file, case$geometry_file),
    native = native,
    dictionary = dictionary
  )
  traffic_export(
    day_view,
    file.path(params$export_dir, "figures"),
    index = index,
    input_files = c(prepared = case$prepared_file)
  )
}
```

## Reproduction, source records, and troubleshooting

Place this Rmd in `examples/beijing/`. From the repository root, a fresh R session can render it with the bundled package as follows:

```bash
Rscript -e "source('bdynets/inst/preparation-session.R'); preparation_session('examples/beijing'); rmarkdown::render('examples/beijing/beijing-traffic-report.Rmd', knit_root_dir='examples/beijing', params=list(time_label='08:00', basemap=FALSE, export=FALSE))"
```

Set `basemap=FALSE` for fully offline rendering. With `basemap=TRUE`, a verified cached basemap can be reused; obtaining a new background-street request requires network access. The traffic geometry, values, summaries, and validation do not depend on a basemap.

Expected outputs are one self-contained HTML report and, when `export=TRUE`, `prepared-data/` and `figures/` directories. Rendering time depends mainly on the full-day map and figure export. Required report packages are `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, `digest`, `jsonlite`, and `data.table`, plus Pandoc. The bundled `bdynets` source is installed into a temporary session library by `preparation_session()`.

Common problems:

- **Duplicate directed-pair–minute error:** remove or resolve duplicate source rows; do not average duplicates silently.
- **Missing pair–minute error:** correct the declared minute domain or restore the missing observation; do not replace it with zero without a documented rule.
- **Unknown road ID:** check direction and confirm that the source pair matches `edge_id` exactly.
- **Requested map time absent:** choose one of `day_standard$time_labels`.
- **Export directory already exists:** select a new directory so that previous results are not overwritten.

```{r reproducibility, echo=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files)))

  caption = "Original archives and source identities",

  row.names = FALSE
)

  caption = "Bundled original-format excerpts and their selections",

  row.names = FALSE
)

conversion_files <- intersect(c("prepare.R", "run.R"), list.files("."))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    file = conversion_files,
    sha256 = vapply(
      conversion_files,
      digest::digest,
      "",
      file = TRUE,
      algo = "sha256",
      serialize = FALSE
    )
  ),
  caption = "Conversion and entry-point source identities",

)

bundle_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "bdynets")
bundle_files <- list.files(bundle_dir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = FALSE)
bundle_sha <- vapply(
  file.path(bundle_dir, bundle_files),
  digest::digest,
  "",
  file = TRUE,
  algo = "sha256",
  serialize = FALSE
)
revision <- digest::digest(
  paste(paste(bundle_files, bundle_sha, sep = " "), collapse = "\n"),
  algo = "sha256",
  serialize = FALSE
)

cat("Package version:", as.character(packageVersion("bdynets")), "\n")
cat("Bundled source revision (SHA-256):", revision, "\n")
cat("Report computation elapsed:", round(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - render_started, 1), "seconds\n")
```
